::: {#thm-false-positive-prob}
#### Probability of at least one false positive

Let $A_1, \ldots, A_m$ be independent events,
where $A_j$ is the event that the $j$th of $m$ tests rejects its true null hypothesis,
and each has probability $\siglevel$.
Then the probability that at least one test rejects is

$$\Prf{A_1 \cup A_2 \cup \cdots \cup A_m} = 1 - \paren{1 - \siglevel}^m.$$

:::

::: proof

The last line below is @lem-no-rejection-prob.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Prf{A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_m}
&= 1 - \Prf{\paren{A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_m}^c}
&& \text{(complement rule)}\\
&= 1 - \Prf{A_1^c \cap \cdots \cap A_m^c}
&& \text{(De Morgan's law)}\\
&= 1 - \paren{1 - \siglevel}^m
&& \text{(probability that no test rejects)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
